item.title: Backyard Book Swap — Sun Oct 11, 10:00 AM — 1118 L Street
item.description:
Backyard Book Swap with Yolo County Caregivers Collective 2nd Sunday of every month, 10am – 12pm 1118 L Street, Davis
Ready for a new read? Join our monthly book swap! This free playgroup meets on the second Sunday of every month. Bring a gently-loved book or two to swap, discover your mini’s next favorite read, and connect with other bookworms. Our book swap is a great way to refresh your bookshelf, make new friends, and add an exciting new chapter to your social life! We’ll have bubbles, simple arts, and space to play for the little ones. Each month features a different theme and free refreshments will be provided too. Together we can build community around the joy of reading.

item.title: Understanding the California Ballot Propositions — Sun Oct 11, 11:30 AM — Davis United Methodist Church
item.description:
Confused by California’s ballot propositions? Get clarity before you vote at a public event on Sunday, Oct. 11, at 11:30 a.m. Guest speakers Vicki Carroll and Klara East from the Friends Committee on Legislation of California (FCLCA) will guide a discussion on the upcoming measures. • Where: Davis United Methodist Church Sanctuary, 1620 Anderson Road, Davis. • Sponsors: Co-sponsored by the Davis UMC Sacred Resistance Ministry and the Davis Friends Meeting (Quakers). Founded by Quakers in 1952, FCLCA is a nonpartisan, statewide public interest lobby that advocates for California laws rooted in justice, compassion, and respect for individual worth. For more information: sacredresistance@davisumc.org
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sun Oct 11, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.description: It’s 1987 on Los Angeles’ legendary Sunset Strip, where the Bourbon Room is the heart of the rock-and-roll scene. DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM. Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website.
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance.

item.title: Savor: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Robert Mondavi Institute - Sensory Building
item.description:
Join us for this quarter's Savor event: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat.
The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities.
The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including:
Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of DavisSam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development CorporationChutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in SacramentoModerator Ca

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Dec 24, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org

Iama Embodied Community This is a slow and mindful practice that emphasizes deep breathing, body awareness, and nervous system regulation. This class is accessible to all abilities, providing a supportive and trauma-informed space to reconnect with the body.
Sessions alternate between floor yoga and chair yoga (on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday). Stay a bit longer on the last Tuesday of the month and join us for coffee or tea afterward!
Like all our events, this class is free, donations are welcome.
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Graduate Education Application Workspace — Mon Nov 2, 4:30 PM — South Hall
item.description:
Applying to Graduate or Professional School This Fall?
Don't feel like you have enough time to get your applications done? Come work on them with us.
We've reserved dedicated time and space for students who are applying to graduate and professional schools. You'll work alongside GSP, EOP, and USP students who are going through the same process—giving you time to focus, get questions answered, and make progress on your applications.
Each session gives you time to: Set a goal for what you want to accomplish that day Work on your applications with dedicated time and fewer distractions Ask questions and troubleshoot challenges as they come up Share ideas and problem-solve with other students going through the process Make progress on the application you've been putting off
On select days, we'll also have Pre-Grad/Law Advising, graduate and professional students, Graduate Studies representatives, and other campus resources available to provide guidance and answer questions.

item.description:

Source: Davis Downtown

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Dec 16, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Data Science in Practice (talk series) — Tue Oct 13, 3:00 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Beginning October 13, join us at DataLab (Shields Library 362) every other Tuesday from 3-4pm for Data Science in Practice -- interdisciplinary talks featuring researchers from across the UC Davis community about how they’re using data, data science methods, and emerging technologies to tackle their work.
The Fall 2026 schedule is:
Oct 13 – Juan Tellez, Political ScienceOct 27 – Tina Law, SociologyNov 10 – Mike Oskin, Earth and Planetary Sciences
Together we’ll discover and learn from different perspectives on and approaches to data-driven research. This series features a mix of talks on active and recently completed projects from academia, government and industry in a friendly, collegial atmosphere. After the talks, stick around to network with colleagues new and old over light refreshments. This series is organized by DataLab staff and graduate student affiliates.
